title: Etale neighbourhood carrying one proper smooth fibre component
statement: Let $S$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth] and let $f:X\to S$ be a separated smooth morphism of algebraic spaces, locally of finite presentation [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-sfb-space-morphism-properties, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and let $C\subseteq X_{\bar s}$ be a nonempty connected component with its open-subspace structure [def-a1-space-open-subspace, def-a1-space-point-topology]. A connected component is a maximal nonempty connected subset of the point space; connected means admitting no partition into two nonempty open-and-closed subsets. Suppose $C$ is proper over $\Omega$. Then there exist a pointed etale neighbourhood $(T,\bar t)\to(S,\bar s)$, meaning an etale scheme $T\to S$ with a lift $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$, and an open subspace $V\subseteq X\times_ST$, such that $V\to T$ is proper, smooth, and of finite presentation with nonempty geometrically connected fibres, and $V\times_{T,\bar t}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega=C$ as open subspaces of $X_{\bar s}$. Geometrically connected means connected after every extension of the fibre field. Finite presentation includes quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. The ambient $X\to S$ need not be quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 0CWI, lemma-split-off-proper-part-henselian, applied to a finite-type open neighbourhood of the proper component after strict localization; Tag 0E1E, lemma-proper-flat-geom-red, for local constancy of the number of geometric components. Spreading the proper open uses spaces-limits.tex Tag 0827, lemma-descend-opens, and Tag 08K1, lemma-eventually-proper. This etale-neighbourhood consequence is an agent assembly, not the verbatim statement of 0CWI.

proof.text: Replace $S$ by an affine open neighbourhood $S_0$ of $s=\operatorname{im}\bar s$; any neighbourhood produced over $S_0$ is also etale over $S$. For each point in the image of $C\to X_{S_0}$, take an affine open in a scheme etale atlas of $X_{S_0}$ mapping to that point [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Its image is a quasi-compact open subspace by [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image]. The image of $|C|$ is quasi-compact, since $C$ is proper, hence quasi-compact, and point maps are continuous [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties, lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. Finitely many such images therefore cover it. Their union $U\subseteq X_{S_0}$ is a quasi-compact open subspace, with a finite union of the chosen affine charts as a quasi-compact atlas. Its geometric fibre contains all of $C$ as a subspace; $C$ remains a connected component of $U_{\bar s}$ since it is connected and clopen in $X_{\bar s}$. The ambient $X$ has not been assumed quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 04NN, lemma-space-locally-quasi-compact, expanded by finite atlas images; Tags 03BZ and 06NF.

proof.text: The restricted map $U\to S_0$ is smooth and locally finitely presented: etale charts of an open subspace are charts of the ambient space, so the chart tests simply restrict [def-a1-space-open-subspace, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. It is separated: its diagonal is the pullback of the closed diagonal of $X_{S_0}\to S_0$ to $U\times_{S_0}U$ [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition]. Closed immersions are quasi-compact (on an affine scheme test they are spectra of quotient rings). Thus this diagonal is quasi-compact. Since $S_0$ is affine, [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-source-products] makes $U$ quasi-separated; its product with any affine scheme over $S_0$ is then quasi-compact. This is precisely quasi-compactness of $U\to S_0$. Consequently $U\to S_0$ is of finite presentation, by local finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness, and is of finite type. Restriction of the scheme chart properties is also covered by [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties].

source.place: Separatedness via the diagonal and finite presentation: definitions separated, locally-finite-presentation and finite-presentation; finite-presentation is qc, qs and lfp.

proof.text: Let $A=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{S_0,\bar s}$ be the affine pointed-neighbourhood colimit [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. By [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-local-structure] it is a strictly henselian local ring, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. The pointed map [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-pointed-map] identifies $A/\mathfrak m$ with the relative separable closure $K\subseteq\Omega$ of $\kappa(s)$; this field is separably closed by [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure]. The equality here is the quotient isomorphism induced by the surjective map in that node. Its pointed equations ensure that the composite $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}A\to S_0$ is the original $\bar s$, and that the limit projections give the specified lifts to all the neighbourhoods. Put $U_A=U\times_{S_0}\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $U_K=U_A\times_AK$. The map $U_K\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is separated and finitely presented by [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition, lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality].

source.place: Tag 04HX, lemma-describe-etale-local-ring; algebra.tex, construction of strict henselization with prescribed separable residue field.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-sepclosed-components-base-change] to $U_K$ and $\Omega/K$. It gives an open-and-closed component $D\subseteq U_K$ with $D_\Omega=C$ as open subspaces. Its point space is the continuous image of $|C|$, so it is quasi-compact. It is separated and locally of finite type over $K$ by restriction from $U_K$; the same diagonal and product argument as in Step 2 makes it finite type. The field extension $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is fpqc: it is affine and surjective, and flat since every vector space over a field is flat. Properness of $C$ implies universal closedness of $D_\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-fpqc-descend-universally-closed] to obtain universal closedness of $D\to\operatorname{Spec}K$. Together with separatedness and finite type this proves that $D$ is proper. This uses fpqc descent, without claiming that $\Omega/K$ is of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 0A12 and the open surjection in its proof; spaces-descent.tex Tag 041O, lemma-descending-property-universally-closed.

proof.text: The base change $U_A\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is separated and of finite presentation, hence finite type [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition, lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]. The maximal-ideal pair $(A,\mathfrak m)$ is henselian by the definition of strictly henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-henselian-proper-clopen-lift] to $U_A$, this pair, and the proper clopen $D\subseteq U_K$. It supplies a clopen subspace $W\subseteq U_A$, proper over $A$, with $W_K=D$. In particular $W_\Omega=C$. Properness makes $W$ quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 0CWI, lemma-split-off-proper-part-henselian, with I equal to the maximal ideal.

proof.text: The small cofiltered category in [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] can be reindexed by a small nonempty directed set without changing its limit, by [lem-weil-pbc-cofiltered-limit-directed-reindex]. Write the resulting affine pointed etale neighbourhoods as $(T_i,\bar t_i)$ and their limit as $\operatorname{Spec}A$. All transitions are affine, since they are morphisms between affine schemes. Restrict to the tail above one index $i_0$, and set $U_i=U\times_{S_0}T_i$. These spaces are qcqs by finite-presentation base change and [lem-sfb-space-fp-qcqs-source]; their transitions are affine, since base changes of affine morphisms are affine on every scheme test. Base change commutes with their limit by [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages], so $U_A=\varprojlim U_i$.

source.place: Tag 07SF, lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit; the affine-neighbourhood inverse limit of etale-cohomology.tex Tag 04HX.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-limit-open-cover-descent] to the finite covering $(W,U_A)$ of $U_A$. Both are quasi-compact open subspaces, so at some stage it gives a quasi-compact open $V_i\subseteq U_i$ whose pullback to $U_A$ is exactly $W$. This use of the cover theorem does not require the complement of $W$ to descend. The map $V_i\to T_i$ is locally finitely presented and separated by the same restriction-of-charts and diagonal argument as Step 2. It is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-source-products], since $V_i$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $T_i$ is affine. Thus it is finitely presented. Its pullback $W\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is proper; [lem-sfb-space-eventually-proper] therefore makes $V_j=V_i\times_{T_i}T_j\to T_j$ proper at a later index $j$. The map remains an open subspace of $U_j\subseteq X_{T_j}$, and its fibre along $\bar t_j:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T_j$ is $W_\Omega=C$, by Step 3's pointed equations.

source.place: Tag 0827, lemma-descend-opens (via a two-open cover); Tag 08K1, lemma-eventually-proper.

proof.text: The open $V_j\subseteq X_{T_j}$ is smooth over $T_j$ by [lem-sfb-space-smooth-surjective-fppf-locality] and restriction of its smooth chart maps. Apply [lem-pc-smooth-flat] to these scheme charts and [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test] to infer flatness of $V_j\to T_j$. Its geometric fibres are reduced by [lem-sfb-space-smooth-reduced-locality], applied after field base change; fields are reduced. Hence [lem-sfb-space-proper-flat-geometric-component-count] applies to this proper flat finitely presented map. At the image $t_j$ of $\bar t_j$ the component count is one: its geometric fibre over the given algebraically closed $\Omega$ is the nonempty connected $C$, and that node permits any algebraically closed extension. The locus where the count is one is an open neighbourhood $T\subseteq T_j$ of $t_j$. Set $V=V_j\times_{T_j}T$. The same node says that every fibre of $V\to T$ is nonempty and geometrically connected.

source.place: Tag 0E1E, lemma-proper-flat-geom-red; smooth-flat: spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 04TA; smooth reducedness: spaces-properties.tex, reducedness under smooth maps.

proof.text: The lift $\bar t_j$ factors through $T$ because its unique point belongs to this open. Its composite $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ lies over the original $\bar s$. An open subscheme of an etale neighbourhood is still etale by the source-locality statement [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties]. Properness and finite presentation of $V\to T$ follow by base change [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality], and smoothness by [lem-sfb-space-smooth-surjective-fppf-locality]. The open inclusion $V\subseteq X_T$ is the pullback of the preceding open inclusion, and its $\bar t$-fibre equals $C$ with the inherited open structure [def-a1-space-open-subspace]. These are all the required conclusions.

source.place: Etale-neighbourhood assembly after Tags 0827 and 08K1; restriction to an open base and fibre-product associativity.

proof_origin.place: Assembly of Tags 0CWI and 0E1E with spaces-limits.tex Tags 0827 and 08K1, using strict localization and 0A12 for the prescribed geometric component.

No repair note exists, so the re-split rule does not apply. Item statement unchanged; the local-Noetherian hypothesis goes unused, which is harmless. S1: quasi-compactness is tested on affine schemes, so |C| is compact; finitely many qc chart images form a qc open U. S2: U→S0 is separated through the monomorphism diagonal, qs, then qc by qcqs-source-products, hence fp. S3: strictly henselian A; the pointed map gives A/m≅K separably closed and U_K⊗Ω=U_s̄. S4: new node 1 (=0A12) gives a clopen D with D_Ω=C; D is qc and finite type; universal closedness descends by fpqc along Spec Ω→Spec K, which is flat and surjective onto the single affine. Using fpqc rather than fppf is needed because Ω/K may be transcendental. S5: the 0CWI lift is verbatim, with (A,m) henselian and U_A separated of finite type. S6: directed reindex, qcqs U_i, U_A=lim U_j from the last clause of the limits node. S7: open-cover descent on (W,U_A), then eventually-proper with V_i×_{T_i}Spec A=W; the t̄_j-fibre is C. S8: flat and reduced geometric fibres; new node 2 (=0E1E over a scheme) gives an open count-1 locus with nonempty geometrically connected fibres. S9: étale composite and base change. New nodes: neither restates the item. Both are statement-only and self-contained, and neither duplicates the scheme versions (lem-weil-pbc-sepclosed-field-components-bijection, lem-weil-pbc-proper-flat-geometric-components-locally-constant); tested on empty Z, on Spec C over R, and on x^2=t. lean.statement: theorem exists_proper_smooth_component_neighbourhood {S : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian S] (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace (Over.mk (𝟙 S))) (hf_sep : MapIsSeparated f) (hf_sm : MapIsLocally (@Smooth) f) (hf_lfp : MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation f) (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S) (Copen : OpenSubspace (enlargedFibreProduct f (smoothComponentBaseMap s))) (C : AlgebraicSpace S) (eC : C.obj.obj ≅ Copen.val.toFunctor) (iC : C ⟶ enlargedFibreProduct f (smoothComponentBaseMap s)) (hiC : iC.hom.hom = eC.hom ≫ Copen.val.ι) (hC : ∃ c : Point (enlargedFibreProduct f (smoothComponentBaseMap s)).obj.obj, pointImage Copen.val.ι = connectedComponent c) (hC_proper : MapIsProper (iC ≫ smoothComponentFibreSnd f (smoothComponentBaseMap s))) : ∃ (T : Scheme.{u}) (t : T ⟶ S) (_ : Etale t) (st : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ T) (hst : st ≫ t = s) (Vopen : OpenSubspace (enlargedFibreProduct f (smoothComponentBaseMap t))) (V : AlgebraicSpace S) (eV : V.obj.obj ≅ Vopen.val.toFunctor) (iV : V ⟶ enlargedFibreProduct f (smoothComponentBaseMap t)), iV.hom.hom = eV.hom ≫ Vopen.val.ι ∧ ∃ p : V ⟶ schemeSpace (Over.mk t), p = iV ≫ smoothComponentFibreSnd f (smoothComponentBaseMap t) ∧ MapIsProper p ∧ MapIsLocally (@Smooth) p ∧ MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation p ∧ MapIsQuasiCompact p.hom.hom ∧ MapIsQuasiCompact (Limits.pullback.diagonal p.hom.hom) ∧ (∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] (z : Spec (.of K) ⟶ T) (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra K L], ConnectedSpace (Point (enlargedFibreProduct p (smoothComponentTestMap t (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)) ≫ z))).obj.obj)) ∧ ∃ k : C ⟶ V, k.hom.hom ≫ iV.hom.hom ≫ (Limits.pullback.fst f.hom (smoothComponentBaseMap t).hom).hom = iC.hom.hom ≫ (Limits.pullback.fst f.hom (smoothComponentBaseMap s).hom).hom ∧ IsPullback k (iC ≫ smoothComponentFibreSnd f (smoothComponentBaseMap s)) p (smoothComponentSchemeMap (Over.homMk st hst))
